Null searches carry a star and their resolution (e.g. '2^26 seeds per cell, resolution ~2^-26'). (3) Quotes are verbatim with the checkers' corrections applied inline (line numbers, dates, 'updated' vs 'added', the mir 'two FAIL lines' fact, nmhash32's last algorithmic commit, rurban README line 259, fasthash source line numbers, whitespace of the SMHasher3 'Average' line). Multiple quotes in one field are separated by ' | ' as in claims.json. (4) Could not be verified: spooky32's claims record had NO checker pass (claims_check null); its official quotes are therefore taken from the checked spookyhash2 record (claims.json row 13) and the one extra page sentence ('just use the bottom n bits') plus the 32-bit-specific SMHasher3 (pass 250/250, 60.20, 4.40) and rurban SpookyV2_32 (13626.51, 56.19, GOOD, no quality problems) numbers were checked by this assembler against the local SMHasher3 tree and the saved README/doc copies only. For spooky32 the verifier reproduced only the 2^30 h1=h2 model (both pairs); the claimant's 2^32 server run and the independent-seed-word runs are unreproduced, and the exact 1/2 balance is unproved (measured 0.4999998 at 2^32). For nmhash32 the L<=7 exclusion argument, the 8-byte fold histogram (161/2^32), the 24-byte null and the generic scans are claimant only. For pengyhash the generic scan (2000 cells x 2^26, 0 hits) and the '<32 bytes cannot beat 2 bits' heuristic are claimant only. For mir the 24-byte pair and the cross-length 7-vs-8-byte half-seed pair are claimant only. For mx3 and fasthash no scans were run (0 bits is the metric floor). (5) bits_kind: 'exact' where the collision event is proved for every seed (pengyhash, nmhash32x, mx3, mir, fasthash) or exhaustively counted over the whole seed space (nmhash32, 1078944392/2^32 reproduced by the verifier); 'measured' for spooky32 (sampled, unproved balance). Scores use L = ceil(max(len)/8) and admit unequal lengths; the equal-length floors are given in pair_kind (mx3 1 bit, fasthash 1 bit, mir 1 bit at the p2 site). (6) Consequence for an existing row: the spooky32 275-byte pair collides the full 768-bit state, so the SpookyHash2-64 row's 6.17 (L=36) becomes 6.13 (L=35) if consistency is wanted. (7) Threat model: every pair is under the hash's own seed argument, uniform and hidden; no default constants. Seed-width caveats: nmhash32/nmhash32x take a 32-bit seed (eps capped at 2^-32 by guessing), upstream fasthash32 takes a 32-bit seed while SMHasher3 feeds 64 bits to both widths, Spooky's native Hash32 takes a 32-bit seed while SMHasher3 duplicates a 64-bit seed. (8) Version caveats: the task labelled pengyhash v0.2; v0.3 (SMHasher3, 0x861A1254) was attacked and rurban tests v0.2; rurban tests mx3 v1.0.0 while SMHasher3 mx3.v3 was attacked; SMHasher3's mir code is output-equivalent to upstream mir-hash.h on little-endian hosts. (9) Verified pair files live under experiment/heur2/ (claimant dirs pengyhash, nmhash32, mx3, mir, fasthash, spooky32; verifier dirs verify-*; claims dirs claims-*; checker dirs check-*); these are not yet in the blog's verify/ package, whose README lists eleven directories.

rows.mechanism: Adding 2^63 to Mix word 10 of the last full block is carry-free and reaches only s1 and s9 (exact +2^63) and s10 (+-2^21); V2's End adds the zero-padded tail words to the state before any further mixing, so tail words 1, 9 and 10 cancel all three whenever one internal bit (bit 21 of rotl(s10+w10,22) ^ s11') is 0, i.e. for half of all seeds -- the published 286-byte mechanism one Mix step earlier, saving one word of length.
